Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
32-year-old with widespread flare of known eczema; prescribed stronger topical steroid and oral antihistamine.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Past few days of worsening sore, red, very itchy, dry rash over chest, hands, arms, especially flexures (inside elbows); skin cracked but not weeping.  
• Associated symptoms: No fever, no joint pains, no respiratory issues.  
• Pertinent negatives: No weeping or lichenification reported.  
• Past medical history: Eczema, asthma (uses blue inhaler PRN).  
• Medications: Diprobase emollient cream (dose/frequency not documented), Dermol bath/shower emollient (dose/frequency not documented), OTC hydrocortisone cream (topical; dose/frequency not documented), salbutamol blue inhaler PRN (dose/frequency not documented).  
• Allergies: Denies drug allergies.  
• Family history: Mother with migraine and hypothyroidism (doctor initially repeated as “hyperthyroidism” – conflict noted).  
• Social / preventive: Not discussed.

Examination:
• No in-person examination performed (teleconsult).  
• Vitals: Not recorded.  
• Visual/subjective: Patient reports extensive erythematous, dry, cracked, pruritic patches; worst in antecubital fossae.

Impression:
• Extensive eczema flare (atopic dermatitis exacerbation).

Plan:
• Start Fexofenadine (oral antihistamine), dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Start Betnovate (topical steroid) thin layer twice daily to affected areas for 2 weeks.  
• Continue regular emollients: Diprobase cream and Dermol wash.  
• Advise patient to monitor for improvement; if worsening or any adverse reaction, contact clinic sooner; otherwise follow-up in 2 weeks.  
• Prescription sent electronically to Boots pharmacy.  
• Reinforced minimal quantity (“fingertip unit”) application of steroid.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected: Exact doses/frequencies for fexofenadine and Betnovate; medication reconciliation for asthma inhaler; smoking/alcohol history; occupation/exposure history.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient stated mother has hypothyroidism; physician repeated as “hyperthyroidism” (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Clear; no major inaudible sections.
